title: Capability gateway and profile exposure API schema for model onboarding and version pinning
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Define and implement a new API schema and gateway semantics to publish model capabilities, performance profiles, and version-pin affordances during model onboarding. This work unblocks product teams who need a single, machine-readable surface for: runtime limits (max_tokens, request_rate), supported features (streaming, function-calling, structured-output), context window characteristics, quality/perf profiles (latency P50/P95, throughput, memory footprint), and explicit version pin contracts for customers and routing logic.

Goals: 1) Provide a single endpoint that returns canonical capability and profile artifacts for a given model version and for model families (logical groupings). 2) Surface metadata needed for routing and compatibility decisions (e.g., compatible KV cache strategy, quantization level). 3) Support version pin semantics: pin-by-version, pin-by-capability-range, and fallback variants. 4) Publish performance profiles with stable identifiers so Console and Optimize can reference historical profiles in rollouts and regressions. 5) Maintain strong backwards compatibility: older agents should continue to discover a minimal capability set.

Non-goals: Do not attempt runtime enforcement of limits in this ticket (separate runtime-enforcement work). Not adding a full feature flag system; this is a schema and publishing gateway change with light rollout hooks.

Proposed API surfaces (summary):
- GET /v1/models/:model_key/capabilities -> returns published capability set for latest stable version for that model_key.
- GET /v1/models/:model_key/versions/:version_key/profiles -> returns performance profiles and limit spec for a specific version.
- POST /v1/models/:model_key/versions/:version_key/publish -> internal onboarding call (audit-only) to publish a profile artifact.
- GET /v1/models/:model_key/profile-history -> time-ordered published profiles metadata (id, timestamp, evaluation_anchor).

Key schema elements to include in the payload (non-exhaustive):
- capabilities: list of strings (e.g., ["chat", "streaming", "function_calling"]) 
- limits: { max_tokens, recommended_max_input_tokens, tps, burst_capacity } -> flattened fields in top-level schema for compatibility.
- context_window: { nominal_sequence, recommended_window, soft_window } -> flattened numeric fields.
- performance_profiles: list of profile-ids with human label, short description, measured P50/P95 latencies, tokens/sec, memory_estimate_mb, quantization_profile_id.
- version_pin_policy: one of ["exact", "major_minor_compatible", "capability_guardrail"], plus fallback_version(s) list.
- affinity_tags: list of strings used by routing (e.g. ["high-memory","tensor-core"]).
- stability_flags: ["experimental","ga","deprecated"] and deprecation_date optional.
- eval_anchor: link to canonical eval dataset or eval run id (used by Optimize).

Compatibility & backcompat rules:
- Keep a thin compatibility layer: if older clients call /capabilities they get a stable subset (capabilities & recommended_max_input_tokens). New fields are opt-in and will appear behind a versioned Accept header initially (Accept: application/vnd.redwood.v2+json).
- profile payloads must be idempotent: publishing the same profile id must be a no-op.

Telemetry & audit:
- Log publishes to model-audit with user, commit, and confluence doc link.
- Emit metrics for profile reads, profile publishes, and number of fallbacks used per routing decision (for experimentation).

Security & approvals: This will require a security review because the publish endpoint can expose model internals and eval links. The PR must include a threat model and RBAC rules for who can publish/override profiles.

Rollout plan:
- 1) Schema design + internal API prototype behind feature flag (2 sprints).
- 2) Publish gateway + read endpoints (beta) to Console with v2 Accept header (1 sprint).
- 3) Internal teams onboard to publish profiles (1 sprint).
- 4) Public rollout and deprecation of legacy surfaces (safety window 6 weeks).

Dependencies: router-service for fallback usage metrics, console to display the profile ids, optimize team for eval_anchor linking, and security for RBAC.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical schema is reviewed and approved by API, Runtime and Console owners
GET /v1/models/:model_key/capabilities returns stable capability subset for older clients and the full schema for Accept: v2
GET /v1/models/:model_key/versions/:version_key/profiles returns at least one performance_profile with P50 and P95 latency and memory estimate
POST publish endpoint accepts publish requests from onboarding pipeline and records audit events
Profiles have stable, unique profile-ids and are idempotent to re-publish
Console shows profile_id and eval_anchor for a version in the model details page (feature-flagged)
tasks: Draft OpenAPI schema and publish to internal docs (Confluence link in comments)
Implement lightweight capability gateway service with read cache and Accept header handling
Add publish API handler that validates profile payload and emits audit event
Add unit and integration tests for backcompat behavior and idempotency
Coordinate with Console team to add display fields behind feature flag
Run security review and update RBAC rules for publish endpoint
